title: Mamie's Blues and the error in Morton's birth year
summary: Carew corrects a musicologist who dated Morton's birth to 1896 and places it around 1885, and Morton's age at death.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: No, it was Mamie's Jelly's tune too, originally. That's the funny thing about that. A guy picked that up in London and had permission to put it in his book and comment. He was a very high class musicologist. They called him talented musician and musicologist, I believe. Anyhow, he put that in and he made comments on it, you know, and he commented on Jelly Roll and so forth. And he went on to say, says Jelly Roll, born in 1896. He says he played piano in the same house with Mamie Desdune and he got this piece from her, learned this piece from her, and he went on with some junk. Well now, 1896 is just six years before 1902 when Jelly Roll first played in Storyville, according to Jelly. So he was six years old when he got to Storyville and was playing with Mamie Desdune.

Yeah. He was off only about 11 years, see? Off about 11 years in that little statement. What did he do in 1885? 1885 is as close as I can get. I think that's pretty accurate. It might have been a year or two.
How old was Jelly when he died?
He was 53, I think. When was he 53? 41? No, no. Wait a minute. No, he was 56. 56, that's right. 41. 56 years old.
